decisions: All non-Ring FAA/FCC JSON refreshes differ only in fetched/enriched timestamps; no new model or serial-range evidence.
Ring zero-result FAA snapshot is a search observation, not proof of absent radio hardware or all possible future declarations.

All 13 Ring LLC allocations independently match the saved IEEE MA-L snapshot dated 2026-11-03 (SHA256 e3a8c3a77347ce9c675c72dfb44faebbf916c2370a426ba2dba57e1f570761c1). A fresh IEEE request returned HTTP 418. Snapshot dates are not advanced.
205 Amazon allocations excluded from the scoped CSV. Ring allocations are manufacturer-only and also cover fixed cameras; no drone presence inferred.
No imported SSID guesses, assumed MAC randomization, BLE cadence, inferred radio-cycle rules, domain-based drone identity or Remote-ID disqualifiers.
No verified device locations in this refresh; product announcements and company domains create no live or historical map pins.
The 135-row Ring grantee index contains many unrelated cameras. Only the specifically identified Always Home Cam record is added to the drone/robot equipment catalog.
Domain-list omissions are not proof of decommissioning; CT/DNS lists do not establish service roles, exposure or vulnerabilities.

Collector pagination can overwrite prior data with a partial result after a later-page failure and deduplicates revisions by FCC ID; preserve per-application identity and complete-fetch status before treating counts as authoritative.
Ring excluded from drone-only CSV: the 13 verified vendor allocations are shared camera/device context, not documented drone allocations.
5CFYB9 is the new Drone Cam hardware model, not an FCC identifier. No new-model grant or MAC binding established.
The manufacturer confirms 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi on both new products. Exact channel limits and chipsets remain unspecified; no speculative RF channel rows added.

Historical label mirror offers a machine-decoded QR identifier, but direct FCC/PDF retrieval failed. It is not accepted as model-specific OUI evidence without viewing and validating the actual exhibit.
Ring TAKE white paper provides platform data/key flow; it does not identify the new drone’s precise enrollment path or hosts.
